title: The Verb: The Future-Habitual
summary: The -తా- form of ¶78 is taken up again for its stem changes: geminates simplify, -ప్పు and -ట్టు voice, -న్ turns -త్- retroflex, and -చ్చు becomes -స్- — the same personal endings closing each form, and the negative tense denying them.

rules.heading: The Habitual and the Future — one form
rules.statement: **-తా-** (and **-తున్-** before **-ది**, ¶79) marks a **habitual** action or a **future** one. Context — an adverb such as *రోజూ* or *రేపు*, or the situation — decides which English tense to use; Telugu does not split the two.

examples.gloss: Tomorrow I will go to the village. (future)

sources.citation: Krishnamurti, Bhadriraju & Gwynn, J. P. L., *A Grammar of Modern Telugu*. Delhi: Oxford University Press, 1985.
sources.note: §15.11–15.12, future-habitual meanings and paradigms.

rules.heading: Geminates Simplify
rules.statement: Before **-తా-**, a stem-final geminate is **simplified** to a single consonant: *వెళ్ళు* → *వెళ్తాను*, not *వెళ్ళుతాను*.

sources.citation: Krishnamurti, Bhadriraju & Gwynn, J. P. L., *A Grammar of Modern Telugu*. Delhi: Oxford University Press, 1985.
sources.note: §15.11; class VI stems such as వెళ్ళు.

sources.citation: Wikipedia contributors, “Telugu grammar.” Wikipedia, The Free Encyclopedia.

rules.heading: -ప్పు and -ట్టు Voice
rules.statement: Stems in **-ప్పు** and **-ట్టు** replace the geminate by a **voiced** single consonant before **-తా-**: *చెప్పు* → *చెబతాను*; *కొట్టు* → *కొడతాను*. Before **-తున్-** the vowel is **-ు-**: *చెబుతుంది*, *కొడుతుంది*.

examples.gloss: She tells / will tell the truth.
He will knock on the door.

sources.citation: Krishnamurti, Bhadriraju & Gwynn, J. P. L., *A Grammar of Modern Telugu*. Delhi: Oxford University Press, 1985.
sources.note: §15.11(4), -TT-/-pp- → -Da-/-ba- before -taa-.

sources.citation: Wiktionary contributors, “Appendix:Telugu verbs.” Wiktionary, The Free Dictionary.
sources.note: Future-tense rule 1; class IV.

rules.heading: -న్ makes -త్- Retroflex
rules.statement: After a stem ending in a short vowel + **-న్**, the **-త్-** of the future-habitual becomes **-ట్-**, and the **-న్** is written as the anusvāra before it: *విను* → *వింటాను*; *తిను* → *తింటాను*.

examples.gloss: Tomorrow I will hear the story.
Madhav eats / will eat rice today.

sources.citation: Krishnamurti, Bhadriraju & Gwynn, J. P. L., *A Grammar of Modern Telugu*. Delhi: Oxford University Press, 1985.
Wiktionary contributors, “Appendix:Telugu verbs.” Wiktionary, The Free Dictionary.
sources.note: Future-tense rule 3; class V.

rules.heading: -చ్చు becomes -స్-
rules.statement: Stems in **-చ్చు** (and several related class-VI verbs) take **-స్-** before **-తా-**: *వచ్చు* → *వస్తాను*; *ఇచ్చు* → *ఇస్తాను*. The citation imperative of *వచ్చు* remains the irregular **రా**.

examples.gloss: She will give me a book.

sources.citation: Krishnamurti, Bhadriraju & Gwynn, J. P. L., *A Grammar of Modern Telugu*. Delhi: Oxford University Press, 1985.
sources.note: §15.11(6), -cc- → -s- before -taa-; §22, irregulars.

sources.citation: Wiktionary contributors, “Appendix:Telugu verbs.” Wiktionary, The Free Dictionary.
sources.note: Future-tense rule 2 / class VI వచ్చు, ఇచ్చు.

rules.heading: చేయు in the Future-Habitual
rules.statement: **చేయు** has the future-habitual stem **చేస్-**: *చేస్తాను*, *చేస్తుంది*. In *పని చేయు* and *వంట చేయు* the noun is still unchanged and may be written apart or solid — *పని చేస్తాను* / *పనిచేస్తాను*.

sources.citation: Krishnamurti, Bhadriraju & Gwynn, J. P. L., *A Grammar of Modern Telugu*. Delhi: Oxford University Press, 1985.
sources.note: cees-taa- forms throughout §15–§16.

sources.citation: “చేయు,” Wiktionary, The Free Dictionary.

rules.heading: Denying the Habitual and Future — again
rules.statement: The habitual/future is denied by the **negative tense** of ¶82 — medial **-ు-** to **-అ-**, and its own endings — not by లేదు: *వెళ్ళను*, *తినను*, *చేయను*, *రాను* (from వచ్చు). Past denial with లేదు and progressive denial with -టం లేదు stay where ¶81 and ¶83 put them.

examples.roman: nēnu pani cēstānu. → nēnu pani cēyanu.

rules.heading: Past, Progressive, and Future-Habitual Together
rules.statement: A time word picks the tense-mode: **నిన్న** with the past, **ఇప్పుడు** with the progressive, **రేపు** or **రోజూ** with **-తా-**. The personal endings are the same set in all three; only the tense marker and the stem alternate.

examples.gloss: Madhav is eating an orange now.

sources.citation: Krishnamurti, Bhadriraju & Gwynn, J. P. L., *A Grammar of Modern Telugu*. Delhi: Oxford University Press, 1985.
sources.note: §15.1–15.2 and §15.11, the three finite tense-modes contrasted.

vocabulary.gloss: to do; verbaliser after a noun

drills.stem: **రేపు నేను వెళ్తాను** and **రోజూ నేను వెళ్తాను** share one Telugu tense-mode. What does it cover?
options: habitual action and future action alike
drills.explanation: -తా- is habitual and future together (¶103). The adverb chooses the English rendering; Telugu does not.

drills.stem: What is the future-habitual of **వెళ్ళు** for **నేను**?
drills.explanation: The geminate simplifies before -తా-: వెళ్తాను (¶104). వెళ్ళాను is past; వెళ్ళుతున్నాను progressive.

drills.stem: What is the future-habitual of **చెప్పు** for **నేను**?

drills.explanation: రేపు selects the future-habitual; తిను takes -ట్- after -న్-: తింటాడు (¶106). తిన్నాడు is past.
Yesterday takes the past తిన్నాడు; an action going on today takes the progressive తింటున్నాడు (¶110). Swapping them, or using habitual తింటాడు for the present continuous, misses the time words.

drills.stem: What is the future-habitual of **వచ్చు** for **ఆమె**?
drills.explanation: -చ్చు → -స్- before -తా-/-తున్-: వస్తుంది (¶107). వచ్చింది is past; రాదు is the negative.

drills.stem: **రేపు నేను పని చేస్తాను.** Which claim is true?
options: Only చేయు conjugates; పని is unchanged.
The form must be written as one word పనిచేస్తాను.
This is the past of పని చేయు.
drills.explanation: Noun + చేయు conjugates on చేయు alone (¶108). Spacing is orthographic; చేస్తాను is future-habitual, not past.
Future-habitual denial is the negative tense; వచ్చు uses the irregular stem రా-: రాను (¶109). వచ్చలేదు denies the past; -టం లేదు denies the progressive; కాదు denies identity.
The first three show -తా-/-తున్- with their stem changes. వెళ్ళాను is past.

drills.stem: Which pairings of time-word and tense-mode are correct?
options: నిన్న + future-habitual (*తింటాడు*) as the ordinary match
drills.explanation: ¶110 sets నిన్న with the past, ఇప్పుడు with the progressive, and రేపు with -తా-. నిన్న + తింటాడు is not the ordinary pairing.

drills.stem: Among **వెళ్తాను, వెళ్ళాను, వస్తుంది, వచ్చింది, చెబతాను**, how many forms are **future-habitual**?
drills.explanation: Three: వెళ్తాను, వస్తుంది, చెబతాను. వెళ్ళాను and వచ్చింది are past.

drills.stem: Among **వింటాను, తింటాడు, చెబుతుంది, కొడతాను, వెళ్తాము**, how many show a stem change other than simple loss of final **-ు**?
drills.explanation: All five: విను/తిను take -ంట-; చెబుతుంది and కొడతాను voice -ప్పు/-ట్టు; వెళ్తాము simplifies the geminate. None is a plain root + -తా- with only final -ు dropped.

drills.stem: Which form is the **odd one out** by tense?
drills.explanation: The first three are future-habitual. తిన్నాము is past (-నా- class).

drills.stem: Match each future-habitual form to the stem change it shows.
drills.explanation: Each form illustrates one of ¶104–¶107 in order.

drills.title: రేపు
drills.passage: రేపు మాధవ్ ఊరికి వెళ్తాడు. అక్కడ అతను అన్నం తింటాడు, కానీ ఆపిల్ తినడు. అమ్మ వంట చేస్తుంది. నేను రేపు రాను — ఈ రోజు పని చేస్తున్నాను. నిన్న నేను వచ్చాను.
drills.translation: Tomorrow Madhav will go to the village. There he will eat rice, but he will not eat an apple. Mother will cook / cooks. I will not come tomorrow — today I am working. Yesterday I came.

glossary.తినడు: he will not eat / does not eat

questions.explanation: The passage says నేను రేపు రాను — the negative tense of వచ్చు.

questions.stem: Which forms in the passage are **future-habitual affirmative**?
questions.explanation: వెళ్తాడు, తింటాడు, and చేస్తుంది (in వంట చేస్తుంది) are -తా- forms. వచ్చాను is past.

questions.stem: How many **negative-tense** verb forms appear in the passage?
questions.explanation: Two: తినడు (denying the habitual/future of తిను) and రాను (denying వచ్చు). చేస్తున్నాను is progressive affirmative; వచ్చాను is past affirmative.

drills.romanization: rēpu mādhav ūriki veḷtāḍu. akkaḍa atanu annaṁ tiṇṭāḍu, kānī āpil tinaḍu. amma vaṇṭa cēstundi. nēnu rēpu rānu — ī rōju pani cēstunnānu. ninna nēnu vaccānu.
